sara (eng-runtime): FYI we got a Sev from Jamal on AcmeCorp — p99 up ~800ms since ~03:00 UTC, looks like KV misses exploded.
omar (support): Customer reported an uptick in tail latency and intermittent 502s. Said it started after the model rollout at 02:45.
jamal (customer): seeing lots of slow responses, sometimes 5-10s, very spiky. No change from our side.
li (sre): Can you paste the request IDs? I want to correlate with node metrics.
omar (support): request ids: req_48a2, req_48a7, req_48b1 — I captured three slow ones at 03:07:12, 03:14:29, 03:21:00.
sara (eng-runtime): grabbing node logs now. Early hypothesis: prefix-KV cache warmup failed after deploy -> high cache miss rate -> heavy long-tail GPU cold paths.
li (sre): Running kvstats on the affected pool:
```
$ ./kvctl stats --pool inference-prod-1 --since 02:30
hits: 12, misses: 3982, hit_rate: 0.3%
hotset_size: 27 keys
evictions/sec: 120
mean_ttl_ms: 3
```
li (sre): That's... catastrophic. TTL seems mis-set (3ms?). Looks like a config regression in the eviction policy.
sara (eng-runtime): I see the deploy diff — config: prefix_cache: { ttl_ms: 3000 } accidentally dropped a zero somewhere when templating -> ttl_ms became 3.
marta (product): Oof. So caches expire almost immediately causing massive re-warm. That matches customer symptoms.
omar (support): Jamal — we pushed a mitigation change that should reduce tail. Can you confirm if you see improvement in next 10 min?
jamal (customer): I'll monitor, thanks.
sara (eng-runtime): Short-term patch: bump prefix_cache.ttl_ms to 60000 on pool inference-prod-1 and enable a soft circuit-breaker that routes requests with >2 cache misses in last 30s to model-small fallback. Applying now.
deploy-bot: Started rollout: config-change-prefix-cache-ttl (inference-prod-1) — 6/6 watchers OK.
li (sre): After patch kvstats shows: hits: 482, misses: 520, hit_rate: 48% -> p95 improved from 1.1s to 220ms on affected nodes.
omar (support): Jamal confirming marked improvement, p99 still edges but mostly fixed.
jamal (customer): yes much better, thanks. A few spikes remain after heavy burst.
sara (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: 1) Write a templating validation to prevent ttl_ms < 1000; 2) Add metrics alarm for evictions/sec > 40 sustained; 3) Implement prefix-key normalization + deterministic hashing to reduce key cardinality from some customer-side dynamic ids; 4) Add a background warmup job during deploy that prefetches top N expected prefixes for 5 minutes.
li (sre): Also propose a temporary knob: circuit-breaker that triggers automatic fallback to smaller model or serve-from-cache proxy when per-request miss_count > 2. That will avoid long GPU paths.
marta (product): Prioritize the config validation and alarm this sprint. Warmup + normalization is P2 but useful for large customers.
sara (eng-runtime): I've opened two PRs: #4728 (ttl validation + alarm) and #4729 (circuit-breaker fallback + metrics). I'll paste repro steps for QA.
sara (eng-runtime): REPRO STEPS (for QA):
1) deploy a config template with prefix_cache.ttl_ms=3
2) simulate load with 10k unique prefixes over 2m: `go run ./tools/loadgen --prefix-cardinality=10000 --qps=800 --duration=2m`
3) run `kvctl stats` and `docker logs inference-node | grep KV-EVICT`
EXPECTED: evictions/sec spikes, hit_rate < 1%, p99 > 800ms.
4) apply fix (ttl_ms=60000) and re-run load; EXPECT: hit_rate >= 40%, p95 drop to <250ms.
li (sre): Thanks. I'll also add a small smoke test to CI that runs kvctl stats after templating step to prevent bad templates.
marta (product): We should inform tier-1 customers about the transient impact and the fix. Omar can you draft a short note?
omar (support): On it. Draft: "We identified and fixed a cache TTL regression that caused short-lived cache entries and increased inference tail latency for some customers. Root cause: template typo during recent rollout. Mitigation applied and monitoring improved." Will share in #customer-comm.
jamal (customer): Appreciate the quick response and the blast to our team.
sara (eng-runtime): Closing loop: PRs linked, alarms created, temporary circuit-breaker in prod for groups with high miss churn. Will follow up with long-term normalization plan. :thumbsup:
